title: Match the harness scratchpad root the harness actually creates
action: In HarnessRoots::from_bases (hook_local.rs, the temp branch), keep the existing <temp>/claude root and, under cfg(unix) only, push a SECOND temp root named <temp>/claude-<uid>, where uid is libc::getuid() (libc is already a unix dependency of this crate). Both go through canonical_allowlist_root exactly as today, so an unresolvable base still contributes nothing and the deny still stands fail-closed. Windows is unchanged: %TEMP% is already per-user, so the single root is correct there. Then fix and extend the tests in write_guard/tests.rs: build_harness_fixture asserts roots.len() == 2, which is now 3 on unix — make that assertion cfg-aware rather than deleting it, and add one test proving (a) a write under <temp>/claude-<getuid()>/... is exempt for both Write and Bash, the same pair gh1_harness_scratchpad_write_is_exempt_for_write_and_bash covers, and (b) a write under <temp>/claude-<other-uid>/... is STILL denied with "could not be canonically contained" — the exemption is one uid-scoped path, never a claude-* prefix match.

truths: A write under <temp>/claude-<getuid()> is exempt from the containment deny on unix
A write under <temp>/claude-<a different uid> is still denied
The existing <temp>/claude root and the home memory root keep working
Windows behaviour is unchanged — one temp root
The full declared test suite is green

trace.outcome: HarnessRoots::from_bases adds <temp>/claude-<getuid()> on unix, so the E1 scratchpad exemption matches the root the harness creates
